From the identity $1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta $ with $\theta =x+\frac{\pi }{3},$ we get 

$$
1+{tan}^{2}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{3})={sec}^{2}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{3})
$$

Substituting the above into our integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi /3}\frac{\operatorname{sec}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{3})}{1+{tan}^{2}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{3})}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi /3}\frac{\operatorname{sec}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{3})}{{sec}^{2}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{3})}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi /3}\frac{1}{\operatorname{sec}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{3})}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi /3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{3})\,{|}_{0}^{2\pi /3} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3}+\frac{\pi }{3})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0+\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =0-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
